subject: DPA redlines: residency & certified-delete language — workshop notes
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightBank Legal <legal@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines — residency & certified-delete language

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for walking through the hosted + dedicated options yesterday. Legal reviewed the draft DPA and attached a marked-up PDF (BrightBank_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf). Their main asks are:

- Stronger residency guarantee for EU customer data (we need language that excludes cross-border failover for EU-tokenized data unless explicit consent is provided).
- A certified-delete commitment for backup copies and snapshots with a 45-day post-termination window for certification evidence.
- Explicit clarification around telemetry/log retention — they want a maximum 30-day floor and an auditable deletion manifest.

We understand Redwood's architecture favors tiered retention and ephemeral telemetry, but we need to align on concrete contract language rather than high-level descriptions.

Can your legal/ops team propose precise clause text we can take back to BrightBank Legal? If easier, happy to run a 30–45 minute call to go line-by-line.

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of InfoSec Contracts
BrightBank

Attachments: BrightBank_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — residency & certified-delete language

Elena —

Appreciate the detailed markup. I looped in Laura (Legal) and Marissa (Product ops). Quick answers up front:

1) EU residency: we can commit to logical geo-fencing for production customer data with an explicit carve-out that prevents cross-border failover for EU-tagged datasets unless the customer toggles a cross-border failover flag. Proposed short clause: "Redwood shall ensure Customer data designated for EU residency is processed and stored within EU-located data centers unless Customer authorizes cross-border failover in writing."

2) Certified-delete: we cannot promise destruction of immutable backup tapes at the same SLA as primary storage (some backups are multi-region for disaster recovery). That said, we can offer: 45-day certified-delete for customer-isolated copies + a documented certification artifact (hashes, timestamped manifest) within 60 days of request. We propose attaching our redwood-certified-erase-playbook as an appendix.

3) Telemetry/logs: we can commit to a default 30-day telemetry retention for tenant-level debug logs and provide an auditable deletion manifest on request. We will not delete operational metrics needed for platform security and product analytics (those are aggregated and pseudonymized).

I'll turn these into proposed contract text (Laura) and circulate a tracked-change doc by EOD. If BrightBank prefers a call, propose Tue 10th 10:00 PT.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Rishi_response_markup_20270508.docx

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightbank.com>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — residency & certified-delete language

Rishi/Laura/Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A couple of follow-ups from Legal: 

- The EU residency clause is a good start but Legal wants stronger wording on the controls and proof: inclusion of a right-to-audit subparagraph (limited scope) and reference to region-specific key custody (if BYOK is not selected, keys must be region-bound).

- For certified-delete they insist on a firm 45-day window to provide the certification artifact (not 60). They flagged the multi-region backups concern but asked for a binding operational playbook entry that specifies how we quarantine and remove customer copies from DR snapshots.

- Telemetry: Legal needs clearer definitions between "tenant-level debug logs" and "platform security metrics" plus an explicit list of retained categories and retention floors.

They are open to the EOD Tuesday call. Can you have Laura bring the appendix draft and Marissa the ops playbook excerpts? If you can provide the tracked-change text in advance, Legal can circulate an internal short-list of absolute blockers.

Regards,
Elena

Elena —

Great call earlier — thanks for the candid feedback. Per action items: 

1) Attached is a tracked-change appendix with tightened language for EU residency, including a scoped right-to-audit limited to data location controls and access logs (see section A.3). We added language: "Key material used for region-scoped encryption will remain under region-bound control unless Customer opts into BYOK or cross-border key escrow."

2) Certified-delete: we accepted the 45-day SLA for producing a certification artifact. Operationally, our playbook requires isolation of affected snapshots within 48 hours of request and a removal plan for DR copies; final certification deliverable (manifest + signed verification) will be provided within 45 calendar days. See redwood-certified-erase-playbook.pdf (excerpt attached).

3) Telemetry: Marissa attached a short matrix that enumerates log categories and default retention floors (tenant-debug: 30d; security-event raw logs: 90d pseudonymized; platform-usage-aggregates: 365d). We also included the deletion-manifest template Redwood will use for certification requests.

Please review the attached appendix and playbook excerpt. If BrightBank Legal provides the internal blocker list prior to Friday we can incorporate edits in a single pass; otherwise we'll circulate a final clean copy next Monday.

Thanks — will follow up with the DocuSign path and the appendix link.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-certified-erase-playbook.pdf
